scope: Adversarial review round 1 of git diff 2f4b4d5 -- scripts/migration/parity (+ untracked selftest-link-header.mjs) against SPEC-04 §3 addenda 2026-09-27 ('Link header preloads', 'compare.mjs outputs')

nonBlocking.issue: Missing stylesheet masked by a preload (confirmed with a probe). assetRefs does not tell rel=stylesheet apart from rel=preload. A page with <link rel=stylesheet href=X> on one side matches a page on the other side that has no stylesheet element and only 'Link: <X>; rel=preload; as=style'. Both normalize to the same /_next/static/<build>/<hash>.css, and hashedCssSha256 still matches because the file is fetched either way. Before this diff, a stylesheet dropped from the HTML of a page that sends a Link header was caught; now it is hidden. The HTML-only form (<link rel=preload as=style>) already had this gap. Current risk is low: Next.js emits both forms from one manifest, Vercel ISR posts send no Link header, and §7 visual tests are the backstop. Suggested hardening: also record HTML-only rel=stylesheet refs (stylesheetRefs) and compare their normalized multiset exactly.

parseLinkHeader, target scan: when a link-value has no closing '>' but a later value does, indexOf('>') takes the rest of the field as the target. '<unterminated; rel=preload, </ok.css>; rel=preload' yields the bogus ref '/blog/unterminated;%20rel=preload,%20%3C/ok.css'. That breaks the letter of the spec ('a malformed header adds nothing'), although the effect is an invented failure (a 404 on one side), never a hidden one, and React escapes '<' and '>' in hrefs. Fix: drop a target that contains '<' or whitespace, then resume at the next top-level comma. Add this case to the malformed-input self-test.

An unterminated quoted-string in one Link header line swallows the rest of the joined field, including a later, valid header line ('</a.css>; title="x, </b.css>; rel=preload' gives []). This is conservative: it can only invent a diff, not hide one. Noted for completeness.

rel handling is asymmetric. HTML <link rel> is matched exactly ('preload prefetch' is not counted), while the header rel is tokenized ('preload prefetch' counts). The HTML behaviour predates this diff. It only matters if one side sends a multi-token rel as an element and the other sends it as a header.

liveLinkHeaderCheck looks up manifest.assets[r] by the raw header ref. If the header ref was de-duplicated against an HTML ref with a different dpl form (for example header /x.css against HTML /x.css?dpl=...), the fetched key is the HTML form and the check would report a false notFetched2xx. It also requires at least one page with header preloads, so running it against a base with no dynamic pages fails it. Neither happens against www.growmax.io today (174/218 pages, 0 problems).

Some self-test counts in the verifier's evidence are wrong. selftest-link-header.mjs has 14 cases and I got PASS 14/14, not '15 PASS'. selftest-p5.3.mjs has 12 checks and I got PASS 12/12, not 13. The results were passes either way. The counts should be corrected before the evidence is relied on.

The hashedCssSha256 pin's expected.b value (072d7bf0...) does not match the B value observed now (4377f3cf... on vercel.app). A's value (5cca0cd4..., b22fd05c...) is unchanged by this diff: header CSS refs de-duplicate onto the same two HTML stylesheet keys, so A's CSS multiset is still exactly 2 entries. The pin mismatch comes from the deployed build, not from the harness change. It needs a re-pin with advisor proof after the H5 deploy, or it will clear once B matches.
